full_text_en:
Funing County Xinxing Packaging Materials Factory and Funing Public Assets Management Co., Ltd. v. Funing County Rural Credit Cooperative Union, Qinhuangdao Far East Petroleum Refining Co., Ltd., and Qinhuangdao Lihua Starch Co., Ltd. — dispute over loan guarantee contract

【Ruling Summary】

In accordance with Article 39 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, where the parties to the principal contract agree to repay an old loan with a new loan, the guarantor shall not bear civil liability unless the guarantor knew or should have known of such arrangement. However, where the guarantor for the new loan is the same as that for the old loan, the guarantor's suretyship liability cannot be discharged.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2006) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 236

Appellants (Defendants at First Instance): Funing County Xinxing Packaging Materials Factory, domiciled at Sanyangzhuang, Funing Town, Funing County, Hebei Province.
Legal Representative: Li Zhihua, Factory Director.
Agent ad litem: Guo Yanlai, lawyer of Beijing Runlai Law Firm.

Appellants (Defendants at First Instance): Funing Public Assets Management Co., Ltd., domiciled at East Street, Funing Town, Funing County, Hebei Province.
Legal Representative: Li Guo, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Guo Yanlai, lawyer of Beijing Runlai Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Funing County Rural Credit Cooperative Union, domiciled at the middle section of Yingbin Road, Funing Town, Funing County, Hebei Province.
Legal Representative: Sun Biqiao, Chairperson of the Board of Directors of the Union.
Agent ad litem: Liu Chunhui, Vice Director of the Union.
Agent ad litem: Huang Fei, lawyer of Beijing Beidou Dingming Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Qinhuangdao Far East Petroleum Refining Co., Ltd., domiciled at the south of Funing County, Hebei Province.
Legal Representative: Yang Yi, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Gao Xicheng, Vice General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Wang Yarong, lawyer of Hebei Qinhuangdao Farun Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Qinhuangdao Lihua Starch Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 6 Beihuan Road, Funing Town, Funing County, Hebei Province.
Legal Representative: He Junshi, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Sun Ying, Vice General Manager of the Company.

The appellants Funing County Xinxing Packaging Materials Factory (hereinafter referred to as Xinxing Materials Factory) and Funing Public Assets Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Public Assets Company), in a dispute over a loan guarantee contract with the appellee Funing County Rural Credit Cooperative Union (hereinafter referred to as Funing Rural Credit Union), the defendant at first instance Qinhuangdao Far East Petroleum Refining Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Far East Petroleum Company), and the third party at first instance Qinhuangdao Lihua Starch Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Lihua Company), appealed against the civil judgment (2006) Ji Min Er Chu Zi No. 00022 rendered by the Hebei High People's Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Presiding Judge Pei Yingshuo, Judge Zhu Hainian, and Acting Judge Gong Bangyou, to hear the case, with Clerk An Yang recording. The case has now been concluded.

The Hebei High People's Court found upon trial: On March 25, 2002, Funing Rural Credit Union, the former Qinhuangdao City Funing Oil Refinery (hereinafter referred to as Funing Oil Refinery, renamed Far East Petroleum Company in November 2005), and the former Qinhuangdao City Starch Glucose Factory (hereinafter referred to as Glucose Factory, renamed Xinxing Materials Factory in April 2002) jointly entered into a Guarantee Loan Contract. The contract stipulated: The lender Funing Rural Credit Union would extend a short-term loan of RMB 31 million to the borrower Funing Oil Refinery, for the purpose of purchasing crude oil, with a term from March 25, 2002 to November 25, 2002, at an interest rate of 4.425‰ (monthly), with a 40% upward adjustment, interest to be settled quarterly; the guarantor Glucose Factory would assume joint and several suretyship liability for the borrower's debt, with a guarantee period from the date of the loan to two years after the loan's maturity, covering the loan principal, interest, and the lender's costs of realizing the claim. Article 6 of the contract stipulated: (1) Default by borrower: If the borrower fails to repay the principal on time and has not obtained an extension, interest shall be charged at a daily rate of 0.3‰ from the date of default; if the borrower fails to pay interest on time, the lender may charge compound interest on unpaid interest, etc. (2) Default by lender: If the lender fails to provide funds to the borrower on time and in the specified amount, a penalty of 0.3‰ per day on the default amount and the number of days of delay shall be paid. Article 7 of the contract stipulated: When the loan matures, the lender may directly deduct the amount from the borrower's or guarantor's account. Article 9, regarding other agreed matters, was handwritten as: This loan is a closed temporary loan, to be used for a specific purpose, operated in a closed manner, and the business department shall supervise the payment of this loan. On the same day the contract was signed, Funing Rural Credit Union fully deposited RMB 31 million into the account numbered 2011051433 opened by Funing Oil Refinery at the Union.

Far East Petroleum Company claimed that when Funing Rural Credit Union disbursed the RMB 31 million loan to Funing Oil Refinery, it also deducted interest of RMB 602,875 on this loan. To support its claim, Far East Petroleum Company submitted a withdrawal slip for a demand deposit account. The withdrawal slip recorded: On March 25, 2002, RMB 602,875 was transferred from the demand deposit account of "Liu Li", account number 2011051792, with the words "repay interest" written below the withdrawal amount. The withdrawal slip bore the transfer completion seal of Funing Rural Credit Union. Far East Petroleum Company argued that "Liu Li" was a homophone for "retained interest" and represented the interest on the loan in question deducted by Funing Rural Credit Union itself. Funing Rural Credit Union countered that the funds were unrelated to this case and were used to repay interest on previous old loans, not interest on the loan in question.

Far East Petroleum Company claimed that on the day the loan was disbursed, Funing Rural Credit Union deducted the principal of an old loan in the amount of RMB 25 million and interest of RMB 534,625 previously owed by Funing Oil Refinery. To support its claim, Far East Petroleum Company submitted a loan recovery voucher. It recorded: On March 25, 2002, Funing Rural Credit Union transferred RMB 25,534,625 from Funing Oil Refinery's account, including a loan repayment of RMB 25 million and interest of RMB 534,625. Funing Rural Credit Union acknowledged this fact but argued that the repayment of the old loan was initiated voluntarily by Funing Oil Refinery. To support its claim, Funing Rural Credit Union submitted a transfer check. It recorded: On March 25, 2002, Funing Oil Refinery transferred RMB 25 million from its account 2011051433 by check, with the purpose stated as "repayment". Funing Oil Refinery affixed its seal as the drawer. Far East Petroleum Company did not dispute this check. Separately, it was found that the old loan repaid by the aforementioned RMB 25,534,625 was the principal and interest of a loan obtained by Funing Oil Refinery from Funing Rural Credit Union on July 16, 2001, for which the guarantor was also Glucose Factory, with the same method of joint and several suretyship liability.

Far East Petroleum Company claimed that Funing Rural Credit Union deducted interest of RMB 4 million on March 29, 2002. To support its claim, Far East Petroleum Company submitted two special transfer vouchers. One recorded: On March 29, 2002, Funing Rural Credit Union transferred RMB 2,339,421.75 from Funing Oil Refinery's account 2011051433, with the reason "pay interest to various credit cooperatives". The other recorded: On March 29, 2002, Funing Rural Credit Union transferred RMB 1,660,578.25 from the same account, with the reason "interest". Funing Rural Credit Union acknowledged deducting a total of RMB 4 million in interest but argued that before the loan in question was made on March 25, 2002, Funing Oil Refinery had multiple overdue loans with Funing Rural Credit Union and its subordinate credit cooperatives, and it had the right to deduct the overdue interest; the said RMB 4 million was interest on those old loans. Far East Petroleum Company admitted that Funing Oil Refinery owed other loans to Funing Rural Credit Union and its subordinate credit cooperatives but argued that the RMB 1,660,578.25 deducted by Funing Rural Credit Union was interest on the RMB 31 million loan in question. Funing Rural Credit Union did not submit evidence that the guarantor for the other loans owed by Funing Oil Refinery was Glucose Factory, and within the time limit set by the Court, it also failed to provide evidence showing specifically which old loan's interest the transferred RMB 1,660,578.25 repaid.

Far East Petroleum Company claimed that Funing Rural Credit Union deducted loan principal of RMB 428,500 on May 27, 2003. To support its claim, Far East Petroleum Company submitted a loan recovery voucher. It recorded: On May 27, 2003, Funing Rural Credit Union transferred RMB 428,500 from Funing Oil Refinery's account to repay the principal of the loan in question. Funing Rural Credit Union acknowledged this fact but argued that since the loan in question had matured on May 27, 2003, it had the right to directly deduct the overdue loan from Funing Oil Refinery's account.

Funing Rural Credit Union claimed that the borrower Funing Oil Refinery and the guarantor Glucose Factory were aware that the actual purpose of the loan in question was to repay old loans. To support its claim, Funing Rural Credit Union submitted a loan application for the loan in question. The left half of the loan application contained the information filled in by the borrower, with the purpose stated as "purchase oil", and both the borrower Funing Oil Refinery and the guarantor Glucose Factory affixed their seals on the left half. The right half of the loan application contained the lender's investigation and approval content, with the investigation conclusion written as "agree to issue a closed temporary loan of RMB 31 million, to recover old loans and make new loans", and Funing Rural Credit Union affixed its seal on the right half. The application indicated that one copy was to be kept by the borrower. Funing Rural Credit Union argued that since the approval by the Union clearly stated "recover old loans and make new loans" and both the borrower and the guarantor had affixed their seals, Funing Oil Refinery and Glucose Factory were aware that the loan was a new loan to repay an old loan. Far East Petroleum Company and Xinxing Materials Factory countered that the loan application was filled out and sealed by Funing Oil Refinery and Glucose Factory and then submitted to Funing Rural Credit Union for approval; the borrower and the guarantor did not know that the Union's approval was "recover old loans and make new loans".

Before the loan in question was made, the Funing County People's Government had presided over a coordination meeting on working capital loans for Funing Oil Refinery on December 19, 2001, and produced a meeting summary. Both Funing Rural Credit Union and Funing Oil Refinery sent representatives to the meeting. The meeting resolved: Funing Rural Credit Union would provide RMB 31 million in working capital loans to Funing Oil Refinery; the loan would take a closed form, to be managed and implemented by Funing Rural Credit Union in accordance with the Interim Measures for the Administration of Closed Loans. Article 2 of the Interim Measures for the Administration of Closed Loans, jointly issued by the People's Bank of China, the State Economic and Trade Commission, the State Planning Commission, the Ministry of Finance, and the State Administration of Taxation on July 26, 1999, stipulates: "Closed loans refer to working capital loans extended by lenders to state-owned industrial enterprises that cannot obtain loans under normal conditions due to high asset-liability ratios, serious losses, etc., but have been approved for relief by the government." Article 14 stipulates: "During the closed operation period of a loan, the lender shall not deduct old loans and overdue interest from the special account." Far East Petroleum Company argued that Funing Rural Credit Union violated the above provisions by forcibly deducting funds, constituting a breach of contract, and should bear liability for breach. Xinxing Materials Factory argued that Funing Rural Credit Union violated the above provisions by using a new loan to repay an old loan, thereby inducing the guarantee, and it should not bear suretyship liability. Funing Rural Credit Union countered that the loan in question did not fall within the meaning of a closed loan under the above provisions and that the Measures were not applicable to this case.

The court of first instance further found: On March 11, 2005, December 30, 2005, and March 1, 2006, Funing Rural Credit Union three times demanded payment of the overdue principal of RMB 30,571,500 and interest from Funing Oil Refinery, and Funing Oil Refinery affixed its seal to the demand notices on each occasion. On March 18, 2004, April 6, 2005, and March 1, 2006, Funing Rural Credit Union three times sent notices of performance of suretyship obligations to Glucose Factory by express mail and domestic registered mail, demanding that Glucose Factory perform its suretyship obligations. The mailing addresses were all No. 6 Beihuan Road, Funing Town, Funing County, and the addressee was Glucose Factory. The Funing County Notary Public Office notarized the demands. Xinxing Materials Factory argued that Glucose Factory had been renamed in April 2002, and Funing Rural Credit Union's demands to Glucose Factory did not constitute demands to itself; the statute of limitation for suretyship had expired, and it should no longer bear suretyship liability. According to the industrial and commercial registration records of Lihua Company's establishment, the domicile of Glucose Factory was No. 6 Beihuan Road (formerly Sanyangzhuang), Funing Town, Funing County.

The court of first instance further found: In December 1998, Glucose Factory, as the main promoter, invested production and operating net assets of RMB 26.63 million to register and establish Lihua Company, accounting for 64.37% of the company's total share capital. In January 2000, Lihua Company increased its capital and expanded its shares, and Glucose Factory's shareholding was adjusted to RMB 32,015,968, accounting for 62.09% of the total share capital. On January 16, 2003, the Funing County State-owned Assets Management Office issued Document No. 1 (2003), notifying Lihua Company: In accordance with the requirements of the organizational reform of the Funing County Party Committee and County Government and the needs of equity management, the state-owned shares of RMB 32,015,968 invested by Glucose Factory in Lihua Company were transferred to be held by Public Assets Company. On February 20, 2003, Glucose Factory and Public Assets Company entered into an Agreement on Change of State-owned Shares of Lihua Company. The agreement stipulated: The state-owned shares of RMB 32,015,968 in the total share capital of Lihua Company, with Glucose Factory as the contributor, were changed to be held by Public Assets Company. During the trial of this case, Public Assets Company sold the Lihua Company shares it held, realizing proceeds of over RMB 80 million.

According to the industrial and commercial registration records of Far East Petroleum Company: Funing Oil Refinery was a joint-stock cooperative enterprise registered and established in August 1994, with a registered capital of RMB 6 million, of which individual capital was RMB 4 million (accounting for 60% of total share capital) and state-owned capital was RMB 2 million (accounting for 40% of total share capital). In January 1996, the registered capital of Funing Oil Refinery was increased to RMB 150 million, of which individual capital was RMB 90 million (still 60% of total share capital) and state-owned capital was RMB 60 million (still 40% of total share capital). In November 2005, after the restructuring of Funing Oil Refinery, the state-owned shares withdrew, and the name was changed to Far East Petroleum Company. Separately, in April 2002, Glucose Factory was renamed Xinxing Materials Factory.

In April 2006, Funing Rural Credit Union filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, requesting a judgment ordering Far East Petroleum Company to repay the outstanding loan principal of RMB 30,571,500 and its interest; ordering Xinxing Materials Factory to assume joint and several liability for the said loan principal and interest; and ordering Public Assets Company to assume liability for the said loan principal and interest to the extent of its shareholding of RMB 32,015,968 in Lihua Company.

The court of first instance held: The Guarantee Loan Contract signed on March 25, 2002 among Funing Rural Credit Union, Funing Oil Refinery, and Glucose Factory reflected the true intentions of the three parties, did not violate mandatory provisions of laws or regulations, and was legally valid. After the contract was signed, Funing Rural Credit Union deposited the full amount of the loan into Funing Oil Refinery's account, fulfilling its obligation to disburse the loan as agreed. Far East Petroleum Company argued that it only used RMB 434,000 of the RMB 31 million loan, with the remaining funds forcibly deducted by Funing Rural Credit Union. Far East Petroleum Company bore the burden of proof for this claim.

As to the issue of the RMB 602,875 transferred from the demand deposit account 2011051792 on March 25, 2002: Although the account holder was named "Liu Li", this did not establish that the account name meant "retained interest", nor did it prove that the funds were interest on the loan in question deducted by Funing Rural Credit Union. Moreover, this account was not the same account as account 2011051433 into which the RMB 31 million loan was deposited. There was no evidence that the RMB 602,875 was transferred from account 2011051433 into the demand deposit account 2011051792, and thus it was insufficient to prove that the RMB 602,875 was part of the RMB 31 million in question. Far East Petroleum Company's claim that Funing Rural Credit Union deducted interest of RMB 602,875 on this loan at the same time as disbursing the RMB 31 million loan lacked sufficient evidence and could not be established.

As to the issue of the RMB 25 million principal of the old loan and interest of RMB 534,625 allegedly deducted by Funing Rural Credit Union on the same day the loan was disbursed: In fact, the principal of RMB 25 million was voluntarily repaid by Funing Oil Refinery by way of a transfer check to repay the old loan principal from 2001, not deducted by Funing Rural Credit Union itself. Although there was no evidence that the interest of RMB 534,625 was voluntarily repaid by Funing Oil Refinery, Far East Petroleum Company did not dispute that Funing Oil Refinery then owed Funing Rural Credit Union principal and interest of RMB 25,534,625 on the old loan. Therefore, it should be established that Funing Oil Refinery used that portion of the loan, and Far East Petroleum Company should bear repayment liability.

As to the issue of the RMB 4 million transferred from account 2011051433 on March 29, 2002: Among this amount, the RMB 2,339,421.75 with the purpose "pay interest to various credit cooperatives" was acknowledged by both parties as repaying old loans owed by Funing Oil Refinery to various credit cooperatives under Funing Rural Credit Union, and it should be established that Funing Oil Refinery used that portion of the loan, and Far East Petroleum Company should bear repayment liability. As to the other RMB 1,660,578.25, the transfer reason was recorded as "interest". Funing Rural Credit Union claimed that this amount was interest on old loans deducted by it. Funing Rural Credit Union bore the burden of proof for this claim. Within the time limit set by this Court, Funing Rural Credit Union failed to provide evidence showing specifically which old loan's interest was repaid. Therefore, Funing Rural Credit Union's claim that the deducted RMB 1,660,578.25 was interest on old loans lacked a sufficient basis and could not be established; instead, it should be established as interest on the RMB 31 million loan in question. Since Funing Rural Credit Union deducted part of the interest shortly after disbursing the loan, that amount should be deducted from the total loan principal, and the total loan amount used by Funing Oil Refinery should be established as RMB 29,339,421.75.

When Funing Rural Credit Union deducted RMB 428,500 on May 27, 2003, the loan in question had already matured. According to Article 7 of the Guarantee Loan Contract, which stipulates that "the lender may directly deduct the amount from the borrower's or guarantor's account when the loan matures," Funing Rural Credit Union's direct deduction from Funing Oil Refinery's account was not improper. When Funing Rural Credit Union filed the lawsuit, it had already deducted the RMB 428,500 from the total amount owed, and this Court confirmed that.

In summary, the outstanding principal amount now owed by Far East Petroleum Company should be RMB 28,910,921.75.

Regarding the issue of whether the borrower, Funing Oil Refinery, and the guarantor, Glucose Factory, were aware that the actual purpose of the loan in this case was to repay an old loan with a new one (借新还旧), as seen from the loan application submitted by Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union (Funing RCCU), although the approval opinion recorded therein was "repay old loan with new loan," generally, the application precedes investigation and approval. Therefore, this application is insufficient to prove that Funing Oil Refinery and Glucose Factory knew of the 借新还旧 at the time of submission. However, the application explicitly noted that the borrower retained a copy, indicating that Funing Oil Refinery knew before the loan was disbursed that the actual purpose of the loan was "repay old loan with new loan." Since the application did not indicate that the guarantor retained a copy, it cannot be inferred that Glucose Factory knew of the 借新还旧 before the loan was disbursed. As for the portion of the loan used to repay the old loan, this only shows that Funing Oil Refinery did not use that portion of the loan for the agreed purpose, but does not indicate that Funing Oil Refinery did not use that portion at all; Far East Petroleum Company should still bear repayment liability.

At the time of the loan, Funing Oil Refinery was a joint-stock cooperative enterprise, with individual shares accounting for 60% and state-owned shares only 40%, which does not meet the condition under Article 2 of the Interim Measures for the Management of Closed Loans that the borrower of a closed loan must be a state-owned industrial enterprise. Therefore, the Interim Measures for the Management of Closed Loans are not applicable to this case. However, before the loan occurred, the Funing County People's Government presided over a coordination meeting, which was attended by representatives from both Funing RCCU and Funing Oil Refinery, indicating that both parties were aware that the loan would be conducted in a closed form and managed and implemented by Funing RCCU in accordance with the Interim Measures for the Management of Closed Loans. In fact, the parties explicitly stipulated in the Guarantee Guarantee Loan Contract terms such as "special funds for special purposes, closed operation," and both parties should strictly comply with the agreement. Funing RCCU's deduction of interest of RMB 1,660,578.25 from the RMB 31 million loan violated the provisions of Article 6(2) of the contract, but Far East Petroleum Company did not file a counterclaim on this ground. Therefore, its request for Funing RCCU to bear liability for breach of contract is not adjudicated in this case. After the Guarantee Guarantee Loan Contract expired, Far East Petroleum Company failed to perform its repayment obligation, constituting a breach of contract. In addition to bearing repayment liability for the principal amount of RMB 28,910,921.75, it must also pay overdue interest.

Regarding the issue of whether New Materials Factory should bear guarantee liability, the court held that, as discussed above, based on the loan application submitted by Funing RCCU, it is insufficient to prove that Glucose Factory knew before the loan was disbursed that most of the loan would be used for 借新还旧. According to the contract, the loan purpose was "purchase of crude oil," and it was "special funds for special purposes, closed operation." Funing Oil Refinery voluntarily repaid the old loan principal of RMB 25 million from 2001, and Funing RCCU deducted the old loan interest of RMB 534,625 from 2001 and interest of RMB 2,339,421.75 owed to various subordinate credit unions, all without the knowledge of the guarantor Glucose Factory. Article 39 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If the parties to the principal contract agree to repay the old loan with a new loan, the guarantor shall not bear civil liability unless the guarantor knew or should have known. If the guarantor for the new loan and the old loan is the same, the preceding paragraph does not apply." According to this provision, although RMB 25,534,625 of the RMB 31 million loan was used to repay Funing Oil Refinery's old loan from 2001 at Funing RCCU, and there is no evidence that Glucose Factory knew or should have known of this, because the guarantor for the 2001 old loan was also Glucose Factory with the same method of joint and several liability guarantee, Glucose Factory cannot be relieved of its guarantee liability for that portion of the loan. As for the interest of RMB 2,339,421.75 owed to subordinate credit unions deducted by Funing RCCU, there is no evidence that Glucose Factory knew or should have known of this, nor any evidence that the old loans of the subordinate credit unions were guaranteed by Glucose Factory. Therefore, Glucose Factory should not bear guarantee liability for that portion of the loan. The transfer of RMB 602,875 from the current account number 2011051792 on March 25, 2002, without evidence of its connection to the loan in this case, does not relieve Glucose Factory of its guarantee liability for that amount. Therefore, Glucose Factory should bear guarantee liability for RMB 26,571,500 of the RMB 28,910,921.75 owed by Far East Petroleum Company.

After the loan in this case matured on November 25, 2002, Funing RCCU sent notices of performance of guarantee liability to Glucose Factory by mail on March 18, 2004, April 6, 2005, and March 1, 2006. The mailing address was No. 6 Beihuan Road, Funing Town, Funing County, with Glucose Factory as the addressee. The Funing County Notary Public Office notarized the collection efforts. According to the business registration records at the time of Lihua Company's establishment, the domicile of Glucose Factory, No. 6 Beihuan Road, Funing Town, Funing County, was originally Sanli Yangzhuang. Funing RCCU, as the creditor, submitted the receipts of express mail and domestic registered mail and the content of the collections. The mailing address was consistent with the address of New Materials Factory. At the same time, there is no evidence that Funing RCCU knew of the name change of Glucose Factory, nor did New Materials Factory provide contrary evidence that it did not receive the above notices. Therefore, it should be determined that Funing RCCU asserted its rights against New Materials Factory. Funing RCCU's assertion of rights did not exceed the two-year guarantee period, and New Materials Factory should bear joint and several guarantee liability as agreed.

Although Lihua Company was established before the Guarantee Guarantee Loan Contract in this case was signed, before New Materials Factory assumed guarantee liability, New Materials Factory transferred its equity in Lihua Company to Public Assets Company without consideration, which clearly constitutes evasion of debts and harms the interests of creditors. Public Assets Company should bear joint and several liability with New Materials Factory for the debts owed by Far East Petroleum Company to the extent of the transfer price of the 62.09% equity in Lihua Company it accepted. After New Materials Factory and Public Assets Company assume liability, they have the right to seek recourse from Far East Petroleum Company.

According to Article 56, paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China: "If a third party has no independent claim to the subject matter of the action between the parties, but the outcome of the case is legally related to it, it may apply to participate in the proceedings, or the people's court may notify it to participate." Funing RCCU alleged that Glucose Factory held 62.09% of the shares in Lihua Company, which were later changed to be held by Public Assets Company. Whether this fact is true requires Lihua Company to appear in court for verification. The outcome of this case is legally related to Lihua Company, and it should participate in the proceedings as a third party.

In summary, the court of first instance, in accordance with Article 90 and Article 106 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 18 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 39 and 42 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 56, paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment: 1. Far East Petroleum Company shall, within 10 days after this judgment becomes effective, repay Funing RCCU the loan principal of RMB 28,910,921.75 and interest (interest calculation method: before May 27, 2003, the principal shall be calculated at RMB 29,339,421.75; after May 27, 2003, the principal shall be calculated at RMB 28,910,921.75; the interest rate during the contract period shall be calculated according to the contract, and the overdue interest rate shall be calculated in stages according to the standard for overdue penalty interest announced by the People's Bank of China for the same period until the execution is completed); 2. New Materials Factory shall bear joint and several liability for the loan principal and interest of RMB 26,571,500 in item 1 of this judgment (interest calculation method: before May 27, 2003, the principal shall be calculated at RMB 27 million; after May 27, 2003, the principal shall be calculated at RMB 26,571,500; the interest rate during the contract period shall be calculated according to the contract, and the overdue interest rate shall be calculated in stages according to the standard for overdue penalty interest announced by the People's Bank of China for the same period until the execution is completed); Public Assets Company shall bear joint and several liability with New Materials Factory to the extent of the proceeds from the sale of its 62.09% equity in Lihua Company; after New Materials Factory and Public Assets Company assume liability, they have the right to seek recourse from Far East Petroleum Company; 3. Reject the other claims of Funing RCCU. The case acceptance fee of RMB 228,701 shall be borne by Far East Petroleum Company in the amount of RMB 216,278 and by Funing RCCU in the amount of RMB 12,423; the preservation fee of RMB 219,211 shall be borne by Far East Petroleum Company in the amount of RMB 207,303 and by Funing RCCU in the amount of RMB 11,908.

New Materials Factory, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this court, arguing: (1) The RMB 31 million loan involved in this case on March 25, 2002, was an independent new loan, not a renewal or 借新还旧 of the RMB 31 million loan of July 16, 2001, nor was the guarantor a renewal of guarantee. The first-instance judgment's statement that "the above RMB 25,534,625 was used to repay the principal and interest of Funing Oil Refinery's old loan of July 16, 2001 at Funing RCCU, and the guarantor of that loan was also Glucose Factory" is inconsistent with the facts. First, Funing RCCU's initial lawsuit was for the principal and interest arrears of the RMB 31 million loan of March 25, 2002, and the civil complaint served to us also referred to that RMB 31 million loan. At the first-instance trial, the three defendants and the third party did not recognize Funing RCCU's act of replacing the complaint during court. The first instance should not have forcibly tried the case in violation of procedure. Second, the guarantee for the RMB 31 million loan of March 25, 2002, was provided only after the borrower informed that the principal and interest of the old RMB 31 million loan of July 16, 2001 had been repaid, and that the new loan was for purchasing crude oil, with closed operation, and with the coordination of Funing County Government. Third, the RMB 31 million loan of March 25, 2002, occurred three months after the maturity of the July 16, 2001 loan, and the interest rates of the two loans were different. In particular, when the March 25, 2002 loan was made, the borrower Funing Oil Refinery had already owed Funing RCCU more than RMB 160 million in principal and interest, not just the RMB 31 million principal and interest. (2) The lender and borrower in this case concealed the truth, maliciously colluded, engaged in 借新还旧, and shifted risks, violating the true intention of the guarantor. The guarantor should not bear guarantee liability according to law. The RMB 31 million loan in this case was not used for the purpose of "purchasing crude oil" as stipulated in the Guarantee Guarantee Loan Contract, nor was it operated as a closed loan in accordance with the Interim Measures for the Management of Closed Loans as stipulated in the loan contract. Instead, it was used for 借新还旧 and deduction of interest. Specifically: (a) On the day of the loan (March 25, 2002), Funing RCCU deducted interest of RMB 602,875; (b) On the same day, Funing RCCU and the borrower agreed to repay the old loan principal of RMB 25 million; (c) On the same day, Funing RCCU and the borrower agreed to repay the old loan interest of RMB 534,625; (d) On March 29, 2002, Funing RCCU deducted old loan interest (including interest of other credit unions) of RMB 4 million; (e) On May 27, 2003, Funing RCCU deducted old loan principal of RMB 428,500. The above total amounted to RMB 30,566,000. Funing RCCU's 借新还旧 conduct violated Article 58, paragraph 1, subparagraphs (4) and (7) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, Article 30, subparagraphs (1) and (2) of the Guarantee Law of the PRC, and Article 14 of the Interim Measures for the Management of Closed Loans. The guarantor should not bear guarantee liability according to law. The Supreme People's Court has precedents that where the parties to the principal contract maliciously collude to cheat the guarantor into providing a guarantee, the guarantor does not bear guarantee liability. (3) Funing Oil Refinery, although not a wholly state-owned industrial enterprise, is still a state-owned industrial enterprise, and the Interim Measures for the Management of Closed Loans should apply to this case. In fact, the state invested RMB 14 million in Funing Oil Refinery, accounting for 51% of the equity, while other investments were only RMB 6 million, accounting for 49% of the equity. Funing Oil Refinery is a state-controlled industrial enterprise. The first-instance judgment's finding that "Funing Oil Refinery was a joint-stock cooperative enterprise at the time of the loan, with individual shares accounting for 60% and state-owned shares only 40%, which does not meet the condition under Article 2 of the Interim Measures for the Management of Closed Loans that the borrower must be a state-owned industrial enterprise, and therefore the Interim Measures for the Management of Closed Loans are not applicable to this case" is inconsistent with the facts and erroneous. The Interim Measures for the Management of Closed Loans do not explicitly require the state-owned industrial enterprise to be wholly state-owned. At that time, the loan was executed in accordance with the Interim Measures for the Management of Closed Loans, which both the lender and borrower knew, and the guarantor also provided the guarantee on that basis. The Funing County Government coordination meeting also decided accordingly, and the first-instance court also recognized these facts. However, the first-instance court, divorced from the background of the loan, deliberately misinterpreted Article 2 of the Interim Measures for the Management of Closed Loans, which constitutes an unauthorized and expansive interpretation and is erroneous. According to the regulations and facts, the Interim Measures for the Management of Closed Loans should apply to this case. (4) Neither Glucose Factory nor New Materials Factory received any collection notice from Funing RCCU. When Funing RCCU asserted its rights, the two-year guarantee period had already expired. The guarantor should not bear guarantee liability according to law. According to the facts found at first instance, there is no evidence that Glucose Factory or New Materials Factory received the notices of performance of guarantee liability from Funing RCCU on March 18, 2004, April 6, 2005, and March 1, 2006. The notarization of the mailing does not prove receipt. The first-instance court's requirement for New Materials Factory to prove non-receipt of the above notices is unfair and has no legal basis. The burden of proof for this fact lies with Funing RCCU. Since Funing RCCU failed to meet its burden, it should bear the adverse consequences according to law. (5) There were many procedural issues in the first instance, such as the judge allowing Funing RCCU to replace the complaint during trial, and the fact that state-owned shares only accounted for 40% of Funing Oil Refinery was not verified during the trial. In summary, the lender and borrower in this case concealed the truth, maliciously colluded, engaged in 借新还旧, used the loan to repay old loan principal and interest in violation of the Interim Measures for the Management of Closed Loans, and Funing RCCU asserted its rights after the two-year guarantee period. Funing RCCU deceived the guarantor to shift loan risks. We respectfully request that the court of second instance ascertain the facts and modify the judgment to absolve New Materials Factory of civil liability in this case.

Public Assets Company, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this court, arguing: The first-instance judgment that Public Assets Company "shall bear joint and several liability with New Materials Factory to the extent of the proceeds from the sale of its 62.09% equity in Lihua Company" has no legal basis. The appellant, Public Assets Company, has no legal relationship whatsoever with the loan guarantee contract involved in this case and is not a party to that contract. As found by the first-instance judgment, Lihua Company was established before the Guarantee Guarantee Loan Contract in this case was signed, i.e., the guarantor Glucose Factory initiated the establishment of Lihua Company in December 1998, at which time the loan guarantee in this case had not yet occurred. Pursuant to Document No. 4 (1999) of the Hebei Provincial Department of Finance and Hebei Provincial State-owned Assets Administration Bureau, "Reply on Issues Concerning the Management of State-owned Equity in the Formation of a Joint-stock Company by Qinhuangdao Funing Starch Glucose Factory" (hereinafter referred to as Document No. 4 (1999)), the management rights of Glucose Factory's shares in Lihua Company were transferred to Public Assets Company. This was a normal administrative act of asset transfer and was required by the general situation of the state's reform of the state-owned asset management system, and occurred before the guarantee act. The first-instance court's characterization of this as "clearly constituting evasion of debts" seriously contradicts the facts. Funing RCCU intentionally confused the civil legal relationship of the loan guarantee contract in this case with the civil legal relationship of the share transfer of Lihua Company between Public Assets Company and Glucose Factory, which is erroneous and has no legal basis. In summary, our company has no legal relationship whatsoever with the loan guarantee contract in this case. Funing RCCU's lawsuit against our company based on the loan guarantee contract has no legal basis. We respectfully request that the court of second instance ascertain the facts and modify the judgment to absolve Public Assets Company of civil liability in this case.

Appellee Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union responds to the appeal opinions and reasons of Xinxing Materials Factory as follows: (1) The loan involved in this case falls under "borrowing new loans to repay old loans," and Xinxing Materials Factory was aware of this in advance; Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union's claim of rights has not exceeded the statute of limitations. On the "Enterprise Short-Term Loan Application" dated March 25, 2002, Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union, Xinxing Materials Factory, and Yuandong Petroleum Company agreed that the new loan would be used to repay the old loan. This point was formally stipulated in the formal loan contract by the three parties. It is evident that Xinxing Materials Factory, by affixing its seal to the loan application, was clearly aware that the loan purpose was "for repaying the old loan," and there was no malicious collusion between Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union and the defendant at first instance, Yuandong Petroleum Company. Even if Xinxing Materials Factory claims it was unaware of the new loan to repay the old loan, Article 39 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China should apply: "If the parties to the principal contract agree to use a new loan to repay an old loan, the guarantor shall not bear civil liability unless the guarantor knew or should have known. If the new loan and the old loan have the same guarantor, the preceding paragraph shall not apply." Xinxing Materials Factory should bear the guaranty liability. Upon loan maturity, Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union issued a reminder notice and notarized the reminder to Xinxing Materials Factory, which did not exceed the statute of limitations. Legal basis: 1. The Supreme People's Court's Reply to the Request for Instructions on the Methods and Procedures for Creditors to Assert Rights Against Guarantors During the Guaranty Period (No. [2002] Min Er Ta Zi No. 32) dated November 22, 2002; 2. The Supreme People's Court's Reply to the Request for Instructions on Whether a Creditor's Sending of an Overdue Loan Reminder Notice by Express Mail to a Guarantor During the Guaranty Period, but Lacking Evidence of the Guarantor's Signature or Refusal of Receipt, Can Constitute the Creditor's Assertion of Rights Against the Guarantor (No. [2003] Min Er Ta Zi No. 6) dated June 12, 2003. (2) The loan involved in this case does not constitute a "closed-loop loan." 1. The loan involved in this case, as stipulated in the contract, was a "temporary closed-loop loan," not a "closed-loop loan" as defined in the People's Bank's Interim Measures for the Administration of Closed-loop Loans. First, Article 2 of those Measures provides that "the lenders are wholly state-owned commercial banks and other commercial banks," while the lender, Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union, does not meet the lender qualifications and cannot grant a "closed-loop loan"; second, from the borrower's perspective, it also does not meet the loan conditions because the defendant at first instance, Yuandong Petroleum Company, is not a state-owned enterprise, and the government has not decided to provide relief; third, from the loan procedure perspective, Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union's loan to the defendant at first instance, Yuandong Petroleum Company, also does not comply with the closed-loop loan procedures. 2. According to the contract, the loan involved in this case also does not constitute a "closed-loop loan." Precisely because the lender and borrower do not meet the subject conditions for a closed-loop loan, and the defendant at first instance, Yuandong Petroleum Company, also does not meet the closed-loop loan conditions, Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union and the defendant at first instance, Yuandong Petroleum Company, did not stipulate this loan as a "closed-loop loan" in the contract but instead stipulated it as "this loan is a temporary closed-loop loan, with dedicated funds for specific purposes, operated in a closed loop, with the business department supervising the payment of this loan." This stipulation is sufficient to explain the nature and content of the loan. 3. The evidence provided by Xinxing Materials Factory cannot prove that the loan involved in this case is a closed-loop loan. Although the minutes of the Funing County government meeting submitted by Xinxing Materials Factory mention that the loan between the parties was a closed-loop loan, the meeting minutes are not binding on the parties and are not the agreed content of the contract between them, but rather a coordination effort for this loan. The nature of the loan between the parties should still be determined based on relevant regulations and the contract. As discussed above, regardless of whether it is based on the People's Bank's interim measures or the contract between the parties, the loan involved in this case does not constitute a closed-loop loan. The first-instance judgment found the facts and admitted evidence objectively and fairly, and correctly applied the law. Therefore, we request the court of second instance to uphold the first-instance judgment and dismiss the appeal of Xinxing Materials Factory.

Appellee Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union responds to the appeal opinions and reasons of Public Assets Company as follows: (1) The facts of this case. 1. The Public Assets Company's claim that it acquired the management rights of the shares of Lihua Company held by Xinxing Materials Factory only based on Document No. [1999] Ji Cai Guan Zi No. 4 is inconsistent with the facts. According to the Public Assets Company's business registration, the Public Assets Company was not established until the end of 2002, and it could not have held management rights over Lihua Company's shares in 1999. According to Document No. [1999] Ji Cai Guan Zi No. 4, in 1999, Xinxing Materials Factory invested 26.63 million yuan in net assets in Lihua Company, accounting for 64.37% of the total share capital, and later increased its capital and expanded shares in 2000 to 32.015968 million yuan, accounting for 62.09%. 2. From Document No. [2000] Ji Gu Ban Zi No. 2 and the business registration documents of Lihua Company, it is clear that before March 2003, Xinxing Materials Factory had always been the largest shareholder of Lihua Company. The fact that Xinxing Materials Factory held shares in Lihua Company is a full affirmation of Xinxing Materials Factory's legal person property rights over 32.015968 million yuan (accounting for 62.09%). That is, whether from the provincial government document or the business registration documents of Lihua Company, it confirms Xinxing Materials Factory's legal person property rights and shareholder status. 3. On March 11, 2003, the shares of Lihua Company held by Xinxing Materials Factory were "transferred" to the Public Assets Company, a fact evidenced by the shareholders' meeting resolution of February 20, 2003, and the agreement between Xinxing Materials Factory and the Public Assets Company, and was confirmed in the approval submitted to the Hebei Provincial Department of Finance on August 26, 2003. (2) The Public Assets Company should bear joint and several liability for repayment according to law. 1. The resolution and agreement (February 20, 2003) preceded the approval (August 26, 2003). 2. This equity change is a corporate act, because the decision-making entity for this act is the enterprise, carried out through a resolution of the shareholders' meeting of the enterprise, Lihua Company, and an agreement between equal parties, Xinxing Materials Factory and the Public Assets Company. 3. The maturity date of Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union's loan was November 25, 2002. Xinxing Materials Factory failed to repay it in full by the due date. On March 11, 2003, Xinxing Materials Factory transferred the shares of Lihua Company it held to the Public Assets Company without consideration, failing to address the debt. The equity in Lihua Company held by Xinxing Materials Factory was formed by valuing Xinxing Materials Factory's net assets, and at that time, Xinxing Materials Factory was already the guarantor of the loan. If the equity were transferred to the Public Assets Company, it would undoubtedly render Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union's claim uncollectible. On January 17, 2000, the Joint-stock System Leading Group of the Hebei Provincial People's Government, when approving Lihua Company's capital increase, clearly ordered that it should "operate strictly in accordance with the Company Law and the relevant national and provincial regulations." However, Xinxing Materials Factory, without addressing the debt or notifying the creditor, transferred all its net assets to the Public Assets Company, violating the basic principle of legal person property rights and the principle that debts follow assets under the Company Law, violating the national policy that enterprises must first address financial debts during restructuring, violating the mandatory norms that even the gratuitous transfer of state-owned assets must first address financial debts and contingent liabilities (guarantee debts), and also depriving Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union of its right to know and its right to object. The Public Assets Company should bear joint and several liability with Xinxing Materials Factory to the extent of the shares of Lihua Company it holds. The first-instance judgment found the facts and admitted evidence objectively and fairly, and correctly applied the law. Therefore, we request the court of second instance to uphold the first-instance judgment and dismiss the appeal of the Public Assets Company.

The defendant at first instance, Yuandong Petroleum Company, stated in court as follows: (1) On March 25, 2002, the true purpose of the "Guarantee Loan Contract" signed by Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union and Yuandong Petroleum Company was a closed-loop loan for the purchase of crude oil, not the borrowing new loans to repay old loans as claimed in its defense. Yuandong Petroleum Company does not recognize the content of the lender's investigation and approval on the right half of the loan application submitted by Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union. The loan application was made before the loan; the content filled in and sealed by the borrower on the left half is very clear: purchase of crude oil. The content of the bank's investigation and approval on the right half was unilaterally filled in by Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union as "borrowing new to repay old," of which Yuandong Petroleum Company was unaware and does not recognize. The loan application came first, and the loan guarantee contract was signed later. The loan guarantee contract clearly stipulates a temporary closed-loop loan, with dedicated funds for specific purposes, to purchase crude oil. After the loan was disbursed, Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union breached the contract by forcibly deducting the loan principal and interest. Yuandong Petroleum Company actually used only 434,000 yuan of the loan. Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union's breach of contract not only harmed the interests of Yuandong Petroleum Company, rendering the crude oil purchase contract Yuandong Petroleum Company had entered into with customers unperformable, but more seriously harmed the interests of the guarantor, Xinxing Materials Factory. The argument raised by Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union in its defense that it is not a state-owned commercial bank and that Yuandong Petroleum Company is not a wholly state-owned enterprise, and thus the Closed-loop Loan Management Measures should not apply, is untenable. The true purpose of the loan should be determined based on the contract. (2) The loan contract of 31 million yuan dated March 25, 2002, and the loan contract of 31 million yuan dated July 17, 2001, are two independent contracts. The first-instance court improperly linked these two contracts together, violating procedural law. In its complaint filed on March 23, 2006, Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union only sued on the loan contract dated March 25, 2002, and made no mention of the loan contract dated July 17, 2001. At the first court session on May 24, 2006, Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union also did not mention the July 17, 2001 loan contract. At the second court session of the first-instance court on June 13, 2006, Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union substituted the complaint in court, linking the two loan contracts together, and submitted overdue evidence out of time, claiming that the March 25, 2002 loan was a new loan to repay an old loan. All three defendants raised objections, but the first-instance court illegally tried the case and rendered a judgment based on this, which is erroneous. By the time the loan contract was signed between Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union and Yuandong Petroleum Company on March 25, 2002, Yuandong Petroleum Company did not exactly owe Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union 31 million yuan in principal; there was no need to maintain loan consistency for borrowing new to repay old. The situation of a new loan being used to repay an old loan was the result of Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union's illegal deduction. (3) The guarantor Xinxing Materials Factory provided the guarantee due to deception. When processing the 31 million yuan loan on March 25, 2002, Xinxing Materials Factory was unwilling to guarantee. At that time, Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union and Yuandong Petroleum Company jointly approached Xinxing Materials Factory, stating that the previous 31 million yuan loan had been repaid. Xinxing Materials Factory was still unwilling to guarantee. Subsequently, Yuandong Petroleum Company approached the county government, and the county government held a meeting to coordinate and have Xinxing Materials Factory provide the guarantee. In the presence of county leaders, Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union and Yuandong Petroleum Company both stated that the previous loan had been repaid and that this new loan of 31 million yuan would operate in a closed loop for the purchase of crude oil. Only after coordination by the county government did Xinxing Materials Factory provide the guarantee for the March 25, 2002 loan of 31 million yuan. In summary, Yuandong Petroleum Company believes that Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union's breach of contract by deducting the new loan to repay the old loan not only harmed the interests of the borrower, who essentially could not use the loan for operations, but more seriously harmed the interests of the guarantor. The deceptive guarantee, shifting risk, and its irregular and unethical commercial fraud should be sanctioned by law. Please request the court of second instance to ascertain the facts according to law and render a fair judgment.

The third party at first instance, Lihua Company, stated in court as follows: Lihua Company has no legal interest in the guarantee contract involved in this case. It is not a party to the loan guarantee contract involved in this case. The outcome of this case, whether the borrower repays the loan or whether the guarantor should bear guarantee liability, is irrelevant to it. Lihua Company should not be named as a third party in this case.

This court confirms the facts found by the first-instance court after trial.

Opinion of the Court: The "Guarantee Loan Contract" signed on March 25, 2002, by Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union, the former Funing Oil Refinery (renamed Yuandong Petroleum Company in November 2005), and the former Glucose Factory (renamed Xinxing Materials Factory in April 2002) represents the true intent of the three parties, does not violate mandatory provisions of laws and regulations, and is legal and valid. This case is a dispute over a loan guarantee contract. Based on the appeal grounds of Xinxing Materials Factory and the Public Assets Company, and the defense opinion of Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union, the main issues in dispute in this case are whether Xinxing Materials Factory should bear guarantee liability, whether Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union's assertion of rights has exceeded the guarantee period, and whether the Public Assets Company should bear joint and several liability.

I. Regarding whether Xinxing Materials Factory should bear guarantee liability. First, it is an undisputed fact that Yuandong Petroleum Company borrowed 31 million yuan from Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union on March 25, 2002, to repay the old loan from July 16, 2001. Although there is no evidence that Xinxing Materials Factory knew or should have known that Yuandong Petroleum Company used 25,534,625 yuan of the 31 million yuan loan involved in this case to repay the old loan from 2001 at Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union, because the guarantor for the 2001 old loan was also Xinxing Materials Factory, and the guarantee method was also joint and several liability guarantee, therefore, in accordance with Article 39 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides: "If the parties to the principal contract agree to use a new loan to repay an old loan, the guarantor shall not bear civil liability unless the guarantor knew or should have known. If the new loan and the old loan have the same guarantor, the preceding paragraph shall not apply," Xinxing Materials Factory cannot be relieved of its guarantee liability for this portion of the loan. Second, although the loan extended by Yuandong Petroleum Company from Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union on March 25, 2002, was described and stipulated in the "Enterprise Short-Term Loan Application" and the "Guarantee Loan Contract," which bore the seals of both lender and borrower and the guarantor, as a "temporary closed-loop loan," the "Enterprise Short-Term Loan Application" also contained the phrase "agree to handle a temporary closed-loop loan of 31 million yuan to collect the old loan and issue a new loan," and noted that one copy of the application was kept with the borrower. Moreover, the fact that after the loan was disbursed, the borrower, Yuandong Petroleum Company, actively repaid the 2001 old loan principal of 25 million yuan by check demonstrates that the lender and borrower used the "temporary closed-loop loan" for oil purchase as a pretext, but in reality engaged in borrowing new loans to repay old loans. Furthermore, based on the facts of this case, this loan did not meet the loan conditions, loan procedures, and loan operation and management requirements under the "Interim Measures for the Administration of Closed-loop Loans" (Yin Fa [1999] No. 61). Therefore, these interim measures are not applicable to this case. The appellant Xinxing Materials Factory's appeal ground that "the lender and borrower in this case concealed the true facts, engaged in malicious collusion, and used a new loan to repay an old loan, violating the 'Interim Measures for the Administration of Closed-loop Loans' by using the loan to repay the principal and interest of the old loan" and thus should not bear guarantee liability, lacks factual and legal basis and is not supported by this court.

II. Regarding whether Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union's assertion of rights exceeded the guarantee period. First, the express mail and domestic registered letter receipts and content of reminders submitted by Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union demonstrate that after the loan in this case matured on November 25, 2002, Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union sent performance of guarantee obligation notices to the Glucose Factory by mail on March 18, 2004, April 6, 2005, and March 1, 2006. The mailing address was No. 6 Beihuan Road, Funing Town, Funing County, and the addressee was the Glucose Factory. The Funing County Notary Office notarized the reminders. The matters recorded in the notarial certificate show that the content of the reminders was detailed and clear, and the legal effect of the reminders should be recognized. Second, in the business registration archives of Lihua Company, which was established mainly with the Glucose Factory as the promoter, it is recorded that the address is "No. 6 Beihuan Road, Funing Town, Qinhuangdao City (formerly Sanli Yangzhuang)," proving that these two addresses are the same location. Moreover, in its defense at first instance, Xinxing Materials Factory did not address whether the addresses were the same. There is no evidence that Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union knew of the Glucose Factory's name change. Its sending of the performance of guarantee obligation notice to the Glucose Factory should be deemed as asserting rights against Xinxing Materials Factory. As the creditor, Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union did not neglect to exercise its rights during the guarantee period. The guarantor's guarantee liability cannot be excused simply because the creditor did not personally deliver the performance of guarantee obligation notice to the renamed guarantor, Xinxing Materials Factory. Therefore, the first-instance court's finding that Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union expressed its intention to require Xinxing Materials Factory to bear guarantee liability and that its assertion of rights did not exceed the two-year guarantee period should be upheld. The appellant Xinxing Materials Factory's appeal ground that Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union's assertion of rights exceeded the two-year guarantee period lacks factual and legal basis and is not adopted by this court.

III. Regarding whether the Public Assets Company should bear joint and several liability. In December 1998, the Glucose Factory contributed 26.63 million yuan in productive net assets as capital to register the establishment of Lihua Company, accounting for 64.37% of the company's total share capital. In January 2000, Lihua Company increased its capital and expanded shares, and the Glucose Factory's share was adjusted to 32.015968 million yuan, accounting for 62.09% of the total share capital. On January 16, 2003, the Funing County State-owned Assets Management Office issued Document No. [2003] Funing Guo Zi Ban Zi No. 1, clarifying that the state-owned shares of 32.015968 million yuan invested by the Glucose Factory in Lihua Company were changed to be held by the Public Assets Company. On February 20, 2003, the Glucose Factory and the Public Assets Company signed the "Agreement on Change of State-owned Shares of Lihua Company," which stipulated that the equity in the total share capital of Lihua Company, with the Glucose Factory as the contributor for 32.015968 million yuan of state-owned shares, would be transferred from the Glucose Factory to be held by the Public Assets Company. Subsequently, the Public Assets Company sold the Lihua Company shares it held, receiving over 80 million yuan. Since all property of an enterprise constitutes general security for its total debts, the act of Xinxing Materials Factory, during the period it bore the guarantee liability, gratuitously transferring its Lihua Company shares to the Public Assets Company effectively reduced the corporate property available as security for Xinxing Materials Factory's debt to the creditor. Moreover, neither Xinxing Materials Factory's gratuitous transfer of assets nor the Public Assets Company's gratuitous receipt and subsequent sale of the assets addressed the original debts of the guarantor Xinxing Materials Factory, nor did they obtain prior consent or subsequent ratification from the creditor. This property transfer infringed upon the rights of the creditor, Funing Rural Credit Cooperative Union, and objectively rendered the financial claim uncollectible. Therefore, the first-instance court's judgment that the Public Assets Company bears joint and several liability with Xinxing Materials Factory to the extent of the proceeds from the gratuitous receipt and sale of 62.09% of the shares of Lihua Company is not improper.

In summary, the first-instance court clearly found the facts and correctly applied the law. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court hereby renders the following judgment:

Appeal dismissed, original judgment affirmed.

First-instance case acceptance fees and property preservation fees shall be executed in accordance with the first-instance judgment. Second-instance case acceptance fees of 228,701 yuan shall be borne by the appellants, Funing County Xinxing Packaging Materials Factory and Funing Public Assets Management Co., Ltd., each paying 114,350.50 yuan.

This judgment is final.
